annotations.title: Climate twin: the city whose climate today a place will have in 2050

description:
The large city whose climate today is most like a city's climate in 2041-2060, its climate twin: "what will Belgrade feel like in 2050". Under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5, with how alike the climates are and how much warmer and wetter or drier the city gets.

For large cities; seasonal means, not extremes. Long-term exposure of a place: get_climate_profile.

language.description: Language code for the name of the place found (resolved_from); the rest of the answer is English

agreement.description: How many of the ensemble's median, 10th and 90th percentile futures name the same twin

changes.description: The city's change by 2041-2060: mean_temperature, warmest_month (the warmest month's mean daily maximum) and coldest_month (the coldest month's mean daily minimum) in C, precipitation in % of the year's

likeness.description: What the distance amounts to: twin, within the year-to-year variability of a climate; partial, beyond it; novel, a future no such city has today; itself, the city's own present climate is nearer its future than any other city's, so the twin is named but is farther

nearest_place.description: Where on Earth the city's future climate is found today, whether or not a city is there

own_present_sigma.description: The same distance from the city's future to its own present

sigma.description: The sigma dissimilarity of the two climates in the 19 bioclimatic variables (Mahony et al. 2017), in units of the city's own year-to-year variability; lower is more alike

twin.description: The city with a page whose 1991-2020 climate is nearest the city's 2041-2060 one
